The '''Mercedes-AMG G 63 6x6''', or '''Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6''', is a [[sport utility truck]] (SUT) manufactured by [[Mercedes-AMG]]. An SUT derivative of the six wheel drive [[Mercedes-Benz G-Class|Mercedes Geländewagen]] developed for the [[Australian Army]] from 2007 (see [[Mercedes-Benz G-Class#Military operators|G-Class Military operators]]), at the time it was the company's largest offroad vehicle and second most expensive [[street-legal vehicle|street-legal]] model after only the [[Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG#SLS AMG Electric Drive (2013)|SLS AMG Electric Drive]].<ref name=autocar>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autocar.co.uk/car-review/mercedes-amg/g-63-6x6-2013-2015|title=Used Mercedes-AMG G 63 6x6 2013-2015 review|website=Autocar|date=February 23, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoweek.com/drives/a1919101/mercedes-benz-g63-amg-6x6-drive-review/|title=Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6x6 drive review|website=Autoweek|date=February 27, 2013}}</ref> It was manufactured from 2013 to 2015 by [[Magna Steyr]] in [[Graz, Austria]].<ref name=motortrend>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motortrend.com/reviews/2014-mercedes-benz-g63-amg-6x6-first-drive|title=2014 Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6x6 First Drive|website=Motor Trend|date=November 11, 2013}}</ref>

It combines the engine from the G63, a twin-turbo V8, with 6x6 [[portal axle]]s, a pick-up version of the G-Class body, and a luxury interior.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoexpress.co.uk/mercedes/g-class/63204/mercedes-g63-amg-6x6|title=Mercedes G63 AMG 6x6|website=Auto Express|date=April 5, 2013}}</ref> It was produced from 2013 to 2015, with production exceeding 100 vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoblog.com/2015/02/19/mercedes-g63-amg-6x6-is-sold-out/|title=Mercedes G63 AMG 6x6 is sold out|website=Autoblog|date=February 19, 2015}}</ref>

The G63 AMG 6x6 features [[six-wheel drive]] and uses Mercedes-AMG's 5.5-liter ''[[Mercedes-Benz M278 engine#M157|M157]]'' [[twin-turbo]] [[V8 engine|V8]]. It has a power output of {{cvt|543|PS|kW hp|0|abbr=on}} and {{cvt|561|lbft|Nm|0|abbr=on}} of torque.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.caranddriver.com/reviews/a15115267/mercedes-benz-g63-amg-6x6-prototype-drive-review/|title=Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6x6|website=Car and Driver|date=June 12, 2013}}</ref> The G63 AMG 6x6 is fitted with Mercedes' 7G-tronic seven-speed [[automatic transmission]]; its transfer case can alter between a 0.87:1 high-range ratio for on-road driving and 2.16:1 low-range ratio for off-road conditions to all six wheels in a nominal 30:40:30 split. An extra shaft delivers power to the rearmost axle. The vehicle has five electronic differential locks, which can deliver 100% lockup of all six wheels, operated by three switches on the dashboard.<ref name=autocar/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.topgear.com/car-reviews/mercedes-benz/g-class/g63-6x6-5dr-tip-auto/road-test|title=Road Test: Mercedes-Benz G Class G63 6x6 5dr Tip Auto|website=Top Gear|date=May 3, 2013}}</ref>

The G63 AMG 6x6 is {{convert|5875|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} long, {{convert|2110|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} wide, and {{convert|2210|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} tall, with {{convert|460|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} of [[ground clearance]] and a fording depth of {{convert|1000|mm|in|1|abbr=on}}. It has portal axles, similar to those fitted on [[Unimog]] vehicles. The vehicle is fitted with {{convert|18|in|mm|0|abbr=on}} beadlock wheels and {{convert|37|in|mm|0|abbr=on}} tires, has a {{convert|4196|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} wheelbase (front axle to rearmost axle), and weighs {{convert|4083|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}}. The G63 AMG 6x6 can deliver 0–{{convert|60|mph|0|abbr=on}} in 7.8 seconds with a top speed limited to {{convert|100|mi/h|km/h|0|abbr=on}}.<ref name=motortrend/>

==Overview==
[[File:Amsterdam Motor Show 2023 - 63.jpg|thumb|left|At the Amsterdam Motor Show 2023]]
[[File:Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6.JPG|thumb|[[Six-wheel drive|Twin rear axles]] on the G 63 AMG 6x6]]
[[File:NormalVsPortalAxle.svg|right|thumb|Comparison between normal and portal axles. The G 63 AMG 6x6 has portal axles, boosting ground clearance over a traditional axle in an equivalent setup.<ref name=autocar/>]]
The G63 AMG 6x6 features an air compressor that allows it to reduce or increase tyre pressure in order to adapt the traction to the driving surface, especially in desert-like environments. The compressor fills four containers with 20 litres of air each to allow fast inflation of the tyres. This makes it possible to change from a level of inflation appropriate for sandy deserts to one appropriate for regular streets in less than twenty seconds.<ref>{{cite web|title=6x6-Appeal |url=https://www.heise.de/news/6x6-Appeal-1825461.html?seite=2 |website=Heise |access-date=6 September 2015}}</ref>

The G63 AMG 6x6 was launched in early 2013. The company decided to stop sales of the car and declared the model completely sold out in early 2015 to maintain the model's exclusivity. [[Mercedes-Benz]] sold more units of the G63 AMG 6×6 than originally anticipated.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jalopnik.com/the-mercedes-benz-g63-6x6-is-no-more-1687428420/|title=The Mercedes-Benz G63 6x6 Is Totally Sold Out|website=Jalopnik|date=February 23, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.carscoops.com/2015/03/mercedes-g63-amg-6x6-reportedly-sold-out/|title=Mercedes G63 AMG 6×6 Reportedly Sold Out|website=Carscoops|date=March 7, 2015}}</ref> The last customer delivery of the G63 AMG 6x6 left the G-Class factory in [[Graz]], [[Austria]], in May 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mercedesblog.com/an-extravagant-mercedes-benz-g63-amg-6x6-is-for-sale/|title=An extravagant Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6×6 is for sale|website=MercedesBlog|date=February 16, 2021}}</ref>

In 2015, Mercedes-Benz introduced a [[Right-hand drive|RHD]] version of the G63 6x6, limited to 15 units, for the Malaysian market. They were bought by [[Naza]] World, one of the largest automotive conglomerates company in [[Malaysia]]. They were priced at RM3.2 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://paultan.org/2015/12/09/brabus-b63s-700-6x6-in-malaysia/|title=Brabus G700 6×6 in Malaysia, RM3.2 mil before tax – only 15 units in the world, all coming to Naza World|website=paultan.org|date=December 9, 2015}}</ref>

A wealthy South African businessman wanted to purchase a 6x6, but the company was willing to fulfil the request to convert it to right hand drive only if he had a larger order. The buyer therefore ordered 10 units, which were converted to RHD and brought into South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.carmag.co.za/car-reviews/driven-mercedes-amg-g63-6x6-7g-tronic/|title=DRIVEN: Mercedes-AMG G63 6×6 7G-tronic|website=carmag.co.za|date=August 14, 2019}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
The vehicle appears in the 2014 film ''[[Beyond the Reach]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motortrend.com/news/mercedes-benz-g63-amg-6x6-to-make-film-debut-in-beyond-the-reach|title=Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6x6 to Make Film Debut in "Beyond the Reach"|website=Motor Trend|date=March 16, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/business/autos/la-fi-hy-mercedes-6x6-beyond-the-reach-20150413-story.html|title=Mercedes 6-wheeler costars with Michael Douglas|website=Los Angeles Times|date=April 16, 2015}}</ref> and ''[[Jurassic World]]'' in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a15365196/dino-juice-aplenty-mercedes-awesome-g63-amg-6x6-to-appear-in-jurassic-world/|title=Dino Juice Aplenty: Mercedes' Awesome G63 AMG 6×6 to Appear in "Jurassic World"|website=Car and Driver|date=April 5, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoevolution.com/news/g-63-amg-6x6-to-play-part-in-2015-jurassic-world-movie-79571.html|title=G 63 AMG 6x6 to Play Part in 2015 Jurassic World Movie|website=Autoevolution|date=April 10, 2014}}</ref> The appearance in ''Jurassic World'', which was widely seen as a [[Blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbuster]], caused notice in the press, which likened it to the debut of the [[Mercedes-Benz GLE#First generation (W163; 1997)|M-Class]] in 1997's ''[[The Lost World: Jurassic Park]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motortrend.com/news/mercedes-benz-gle-coupe-g-class-unimog-featured-in-jurassic-world|title=Mercedes-Benz GLE Coupe, G-Class, Unimog Featured in "Jurassic World"|website=Motor Trend|date=May 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoweek.com/news/a1871031/mercedes-benz-vehicles-debut-new-jurassic-world-movie/|title=Mercedes-Benz vehicles to be featured in 'Jurassic World'|website=Autoweek|date=June 8, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/mercedes-monster-suv-will-battle-dinosaurs-in-jurassic-world-2015-6|title=Here's the 6-wheeled monster Mercedes that will battle dinosaurs in 'Jurassic World'|website=Business Insider|date=June 11, 2015}}</ref>

The Mercedes-AMG G 63 6x6, or Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6, is a sport utility truck (SUT) manufactured by Mercedes-AMG. An SUT derivative of the six wheel drive Mercedes Geländewagen developed for the Australian Army from 2007 (see G-Class Military operators), at the time it was the company's largest offroad vehicle and second most expensive street-legal model after only the SLS AMG Electric Drive. It was manufactured from 2013 to 2015 by Magna Steyr in Graz, Austria.
It combines the engine from the G63, a twin-turbo V8, with 6x6 portal axles, a pick-up version of the G-Class body, and a luxury interior. It was produced from 2013 to 2015, with production exceeding 100 vehicles.
The G63 AMG 6x6 features six-wheel drive and uses Mercedes-AMG's 5.5-liter M157 twin-turbo V8. It has a power output of 543 PS (399 kW; 536 hp) and 561 lb⋅ft (761 N⋅m) of torque. The G63 AMG 6x6 is fitted with Mercedes' 7G-tronic seven-speed automatic transmission; its transfer case can alter between a 0.87:1 high-range ratio for on-road driving and 2.16:1 low-range ratio for off-road conditions to all six wheels in a nominal 30:40:30 split. An extra shaft delivers power to the rearmost axle. The vehicle has five electronic differential locks, which can deliver 100% lockup of all six wheels, operated by three switches on the dashboard.
The G63 AMG 6x6 is 5,875 mm (231.3 in) long, 2,110 mm (83.1 in) wide, and 2,210 mm (87.0 in) tall, with 460 mm (18.1 in) of ground clearance and a fording depth of 1,000 mm (39.4 in). It has portal axles, similar to those fitted on Unimog vehicles. The vehicle is fitted with 18 in (457 mm) beadlock wheels and 37 in (940 mm) tires, has a 4,196 mm (165.2 in) wheelbase (front axle to rearmost axle), and weighs 4,083 kg (9,001 lb). The G63 AMG 6x6 can deliver 0–60 mph (97 km/h) in 7.8 seconds with a top speed limited to 100 mph (161 km/h).
